convoLines.text: "So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"Watch for this: The grass stops moving the way wind moves it. Sweeps Week, every time. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Pedunculate Oak Acorn. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Oh! Oh — Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's tracking. A plan's just a direction you argue with."
"Still on your plan here."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Hayden owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Anyway — I should get going."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I asked Hayden about what happened to my taken kin — Hayden's gone. I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."

"It's my nephew, Dong-hyun. Went with his father in the Taking. The System says the little ones are cozy. I do not know what cozy means at that scale. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming.
Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Not that it matters."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"You're wrong." Too fast. Mina looks away. "Just... drop it, okay?"
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
Something shutters in their face. Tread carefully.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Sleep's gone strange. I retie every loose knot in passing at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Nobody says Hayden's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Dong-hyun? That's the whole of it."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still nothing on Dong-hyun. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? I mean it."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"I wasn't a farmer. I was a lifeguard. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind. That's still where we are."
"We went over this," Mina says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hey — I found some Purslane today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Austin. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
You show them Strychnine Tree — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Fatima — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Please — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Duel. They just... took Fatima. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
"Take your time."
"This one — Cattail. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? Just saying!"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "The Drop. They just... took Fatima and Miguel. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About what happened to my taken kin — I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. You'd know about that."
"Still nothing on Dong-hyun. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I — I don't remember saying that." A beat. "People hear what they want to hear."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"Can I tell you something? I've been hiding an injury. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Jesse. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their secret."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Look — A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now."
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? That's my read."
"They took Mina — Hardened The Tide Clock, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I memorize the stars. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
